name: Omni Homestead
positioning: The Omni Homestead Resort & Spa: a historic resort and National Historic Landmark in Virginia's Allegheny Mountains, first built as a hotel in 1766, with its own historic warm springs bathhouses
best_for: Golfers who want two courses, including the nation's oldest first tee in continuous use
Families who want a water park and year-round outdoor activities
Travelers drawn to historic mineral springs and bathhouses

facts.text: The resort is set in Western Virginia in the Allegheny Mountains.
The resort has been designated a National Historic Landmark and makes up most of the town of Hot Springs, Virginia.
Thomas Bullitt built the first hotel on the site of the resort in 1766.
The current resort dates to 1902, when M.E. Ingalls redeveloped the grounds after a fire destroyed the original structure.
In the Great Hall, a custom pink carpet nods to the flora and fauna of the surrounding Allegheny Mountains.
The resort has two golf courses, The Cascades and The Old Course.
The golf includes the nation's oldest first tee in continuous use.
Spa guests can enjoy a river reflexology walk, poolside cabanas and an outdoor Finnish-style sauna.
The Spa has the Herbal Cocoon, a Himalayan salt sauna.
Premier rooms have views of the Allegheny Mountains.
Outdoor activities include four Har-Tru tennis courts, pickleball, hiking and biking trails, archery, kayaking and fly fishing.
In winter, families can go skiing, snow tubing and ice skating.

highlights.text: The original octagonal stone bathing basin at the Warm Springs Pools was built in 1761, making it the first spa structure in America.
The signature Warm Springs experience gives 50 minutes of exclusive access to the Gentlemen's or Ladies' Bathhouse, both dating to the 19th century.
Omni shuttles take guests to a trail along Cascades Creek, about 15 minutes away, for guided hikes or fly-fishing.
The resort has a two-acre water park.

considerations.text: The Warm Springs Pools are in Warm Springs, Virginia, about five miles from the resort, and reservations are required.
Common flight routes are via Greenbrier Valley Airport, 50 miles away, or Roanoke-Blacksburg Regional Airport, 73 miles away.
WhataHotel notes the remote mountain location requires travel planning.
